title: Meet wtfOS
summary: One internet desktop for identity, creation, ownership, play, community, and live experiences.
narration: Hey, I'm Tommy. Gee whiz, wtfOS puts my identity, stuff, games, projects, and people on one internet desktop. In Profile, I can prove my Tezos and Etherlink wallets and connect the social accounts I actually control. Studio gives my ideas a path from a rough project to created, preserved, and published work. WTF IAM lets me discover community-made apps, items, and experiences without losing track of what I own. Then I can play, join events, talk, go live, or put media on wtfTV. I just choose Play, Create, Shop, Events, or Talk and keep going.

title: Play on wtfOS
summary: Discover community games, run owned titles, build new ones, and turn play into shared progress.

title: Create on wtfOS
summary: Move from a rough idea to collaborative media, durable storage, on-chain releases, and live presentation.
narration: Hey, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how I create on wtfOS without losing the project between tools. First, Studio gives the idea a home for collaborators, drafts, versions, and the release plan. Broot and the visual tools help me make images, G I Fs, video, and layered media. Pasta Protocol tools help package collection-ready work. IPFS preservation keeps the finished artifacts and portable manifests attached to their provenance. When I'm ready, I can carry the same release into a gallery, Tezos mint, live stage, social post, or my own wtfTV channel.

title: Shop, own, and trade on wtfOS
summary: Connect wallet identity to collections, community markets, app unlocks, swaps, and portable names.
narration: Hey, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how Shop works when identity and ownership stay connected. First, I prove my Tezos and Etherlink wallets in Profile, and my wallet still approves every signature. My Gallery brings owned media and my own creative work together. WTF IAM is the community shop for apps, desktop items, preservation tools, Arcade access, and creator experiences. Marketplace, trade boards, swaps, and tips give me different ways to exchange value without pretending they are the same thing. I can even claim a portable wtfOS or Tezos name and keep it connected to the account that owns it.

title: Events, quests, and rewards on wtfOS
summary: Follow rounds, challenges, side quests, calendars, proofs, and rewards from one daily command center.
narration: Hey, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how Events on wtfOS connect the calendar to things I can actually do. My Dashboard shows the next move across my account, activity, and daily loop. Rounds organize seasons and their launch boards. Challenges tell me the requirement, the proof, and the review state. Side Quests give me smaller daily actions that can connect to EXP, WTF rewards, unlocks, or recognition when I'm eligible. The Calendar points into gameshows, live rooms, mint moments, and creator launches, so the reminder is also a way into the event.

title: Talk, go live, and broadcast on wtfOS
summary: Move between public posts, private messages, community boards, AT Protocol, live rooms, and television.
narration: Hey, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how I Talk on wtfOS at the size the moment needs. W is my lightweight public feed. WIM is where I move into direct messages and buddy conversations. The Message Board keeps longer community threads, reactions, pins, and channel permissions organized. Skywire connects my AT Protocol identity for Bluesky feeds, posts, chats, signals, and live status. WTF LIVE adds rooms, stages, voice, video, screen sharing, reactions, show kits, and tips. If the moment should keep broadcasting, I program uploaded or owned media into a wtfTV channel.
